notes: §1989:A.2.13.3 AR1 makes argument-1 "a positive integer that represents a number of days succeeding December 31, 1600, in the Gregorian calendar" with no upper limit; 3,067,671 is the 2023 ceiling (§2023:15.5.2). The integer screen (CheckArgumentClasses, IntegerViolation) conforms at 85: DAY-OF-INTEGER of a scaled item is refused with COBOL1627. The runtime body DayOfInteger applies the 2023 ceiling at every edition, so at --std 85 an argument above 3,067,671 returns 0. The witness runs arguments 1 and 366 only. Same caveat as DATE-OF-INTEGER: §1989:A.2.13.4 prints the form YYYYDDD, and the verdict follows the change record and kb/Work PB5130's reading. No kb/Work note owns the fix; PB5130 is the sibling with the same mechanism.

next.reason: 1989: argument-1 'is a positive integer that represents a number of days succeeding December 31, 1600', no upper bound. 2023 §2023:15.24.3 AR1 requires 'a value in integer date form', and §2023:15.5.2 bounds that form at 'less than or equal to ... 3,067,671'. Larger arguments, in range in 1989, are now out of range (EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION per §2023:15.3 AR14). Stricter. §2023:15.5.2 has no catalog row.
